label: Revision-original AQA-aligned practice question (not an AQA question)

question.context: A café has unchanged fixed and variable costs and raises the price of each sandwich from £16 to £18. This is original Revision practice on interpreting a break-even chart.
question.stem: Which change to the café’s break-even chart is correct, assuming the sale price increases but the costs per sandwich and fixed costs stay unchanged?

options.label: A
options.text: The total-cost line becomes steeper, and break-even output rises.

options.label: B
options.text: The total-revenue line becomes steeper from the origin, and break-even output falls.

options.label: C
options.text: The fixed-cost line shifts up, and break-even output rises.

options.label: D
options.text: The three lines remain unchanged, and only the forecast output point moves right.

option_rationale: A is incorrect. Variable and fixed costs are unchanged, so neither cost line changes.
B is correct because price per unit raises the revenue slope and increases contribution per unit, moving break-even output left if demand effects are held out of the chart.
C is incorrect. A price change does not move the fixed-cost line.
D is incorrect. Changing price rotates the revenue line, unlike changing only planned output.
mark_scheme.model_answer: B. Higher selling price steepens the total-revenue line through zero. The intersection with the unchanged total-cost line moves to a lower output; the firm should separately consider whether the higher price reduces demand.
